prompt: What is the lesson's test for whether an architecture page should exist?
hint: Something a reader cannot recover however long they read.

choices.text: Whether it follows the arc42 template
choices.why: arc42 is a checklist of questions, and filled in whole it rebuilds the 2021 wiki.

choices.text: Whether it tells a named reader what the code cannot
choices.why: Right: anything else is a copy of the code, and the copy is the one that goes wrong.

choices.text: Whether a new engineer asked for it
choices.why: A request is a good sign, but the test is what the page carries.

choices.text: Whether the team has time to write it this quarter
choices.why: Time decides when, not whether the page earns a place.

prompt: Which of these questions can Carreto's monolith code answer on its own?
hint: What the code does, line by line.

choices.text: Why Tracking has its own database
choices.why: A reason and the rejected options are what a decision record holds.

choices.text: Which team owns each of the 14 services
choices.why: Ownership is outside the code.

choices.text: How the freight on a quote is calculated
choices.why: Right: that is behaviour, and the code answers it for anyone who knows where to look.

choices.text: What to do when a payout is stuck at 3 a.m.
choices.why: That is a runbook, written by whoever unstuck it last time.

prompt: Match each C4 level to what it shows.
hint: Each level opens one box of the level above.

pairs.right: the system as one box, with its users and outside systems
the apps, services and databases that run separately
the main parts inside one running unit

right_distractors: the machines and networks each part runs on

prompt: Why does the lesson say no single diagram can be "the architecture diagram"?

choices.text: Diagrams go out of date too quickly
choices.why: They do, but that is the third section's subject; this is about readers.

choices.text: Notations disagree on what a box means
choices.why: Notation is not the argument; the questions are.

choices.text: A system's architecture lives in the code, not in drawings
choices.why: True in a sense, but the point here is that different readers bring different questions.

choices.text: Each reader brings a different question
choices.why: Right: stakeholders bring different concerns and a view answers some; one drawing for all four would answer none.

prompt: Paula needs to know what happens when GPS positions arrive faster than Tracking can write them. Which view answers that, and why not the C4 container diagram?

choices.text: The 4+1 process view
choices.why: Right: it covers concurrency at runtime; the container diagram shows what runs and who talks, not how it behaves under a burst.

choices.text: The context diagram, since Tracking talks to drivers' phones
choices.why: Context shows the phones as users, nothing about load.

choices.text: The development view, as it shows which team owns Tracking
choices.why: Ownership does not answer what happens in a burst.

choices.text: A code-level diagram of the position handler
choices.why: Classes show structure, not how the running system copes with the rate.

prompt: Following Brown's advice, which C4 diagrams did Renata plan for Carreto?
hint: Most teams need the first two.

choices.text: All four levels for each of the 14 services
choices.why: That is the 2021 wiki again, wrong after every commit at the code level.

choices.text: Context, containers, and two component views
choices.why: Right: two for everybody, two for Matching and Payments where the inside is hard, code generated when needed.

choices.text: A context diagram and nothing else
choices.why: Ícaro and Paula need the container level; context does not show the services.

choices.text: Code diagrams, since they are generated for free
choices.why: Generated on the day somebody needs them, not kept as pages.

prompt: Why had none of the 1,100 Payments pull requests since March 2023 touched the wiki page?

choices.text: The developers did not know how to edit the wiki
choices.why: Anybody can edit it; that was the problem.

choices.text: The page was still accurate
choices.why: It was not; Tracking had moved out in 2024.

choices.text: A pull request has no way to reach it
choices.why: Right: it lives elsewhere, with no review and no link to the code.

choices.text: Bruno had forbidden edits to it
choices.why: Nobody forbade anything; nothing in the workflow led there.

prompt: Which follow from keeping docs/ in the same repository as the code? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A reviewer sees the code change and the diagram change in one diff
choices.why: Yes: a stale arrow is a review comment, like a failing test.

choices.text: The documentation for version 2.4 is in the tag for version 2.4
choices.why: Yes: history comes with the code's history.

choices.text: Developers stop needing to write anything by hand
choices.why: No: the writing is the same; where it lives is what changed.

choices.text: The pipeline fails a build on a broken link or an ADR with no status
choices.why: Yes: what lives in the repository is checkable.

prompt: In the Structurizr example, why can the context and container views not disagree about which outside systems exist?

choices.text: Structurizr checks the two drawings against each other
choices.why: Nothing compares two drawings; there is only one source.

choices.text: Both are drawn from one model written once
choices.why: Right: hand-drawn diagrams are separate claims; generated views share a single one.

choices.text: Autolayout places the outside systems the same way
choices.why: Layout is about position, not about which systems exist.

choices.text: A reviewer reads both views in the pull request
choices.why: Reviewers help, but the guarantee comes from the single model.

prompt: Sílvio does not open repositories. How does the lesson get documentation to him?

choices.text: Renata copies the key pages into a wiki for finance
choices.why: A second copy is the start of a second, drifting truth.

choices.text: Engineering sends him a PDF each quarter
choices.why: A quarterly export is out of date between quarters, and nobody owns it.

choices.text: The pipeline publishes docs/ on each merge
choices.why: Right: readers read the published copy, which is regenerated and never edited.

choices.text: He is given read access to the repositories
choices.why: The lesson says he should not have to open them.

prompt: In a repository, a GitHub ___ file can require the owning team's review for any change under docs/.
A proposal Renata wrote to get a decision on R1 is a Markdown file. Should it go into docs/ and be kept up to date?
hint: Its job ends when the decision is made.

choices.text: Yes, since every Markdown file belongs next to the code
choices.why: The format is not the test; what the document is for is.

choices.text: Yes, updated whenever R1 changes
choices.why: Updating it would rewrite what was proposed and decided at the time.

choices.text: No: it records a moment, not the system
choices.why: Right: a proposal is a record of a moment, not a description of the system.

choices.text: No, because Helena cannot read repositories
choices.why: Publishing solves the reader problem; the reason here is what kind of document it is.

prompt: Why does the lesson say a stale page does more harm than a missing one?

choices.text: A missing page produces a question; a wrong one produces confidence
choices.why: Right: without the page he would have asked Bruno and had the answer in five minutes.

choices.text: Stale pages take up space in the wiki search
choices.why: Clutter is a cost, but not the one that cost six days.

choices.text: Stale pages are harder to delete
choices.why: Deleting is not harder; the harm is in being believed.

choices.text: Readers blame the author
choices.why: Blame is not the lesson's point; Ícaro's time is.

prompt: A page lists every endpoint of Payments. Another says Payments owns payouts and Tracking owns delivery proof. Why does the lesson prefer the second?

choices.text: Endpoints are secret and should not be documented
choices.why: Nothing is secret here; an API reference is generated from the OpenAPI file.

choices.text: It is written at a level that changes slowly
choices.why: Right: it changes about once a year; write at the slow level and generate the endpoint list.

choices.text: Shorter pages are read more
choices.why: Length is not the argument; how fast the content goes wrong is.

choices.text: Helena cannot read endpoint lists
choices.why: Different readers matter, but the reason here is rot.

prompt: A page's date has passed its review interval. What does Carreto's pipeline job do, and what is it for?
hint: It does not make the page right.

choices.text: Deletes the page, so nothing stale is published
choices.why: Deleting is the owner's choice after a check; the job only flags.

choices.text: Reassigns it to the architect
choices.why: Ownership stays with the team; the architect is not the owner of every page.

choices.text: Puts a banner on the published copy, so nobody trusts it by mistake
choices.why: Right: it moves the page out of the wrong-and-trusted corner.

choices.text: Fails the build of the owning team
choices.why: Blocking unrelated work would teach people to bump dates without checking.

prompt: Somebody edits a 2024 ADR so that its decision matches today's system. What has gone wrong?

choices.text: Nothing: keeping documents current is the goal
choices.why: Current is the goal for descriptions; a record's value is being true as of its date.

choices.text: The ADR should have been deleted instead
choices.why: Deleting loses the history too; it should be superseded.

choices.text: Only the architect may edit ADRs
choices.why: Who edits is not the issue; editing a record at all is.

choices.text: A record was treated as a description, erasing why the system was built as it was
choices.why: Right: a new ADR supersedes the old one, which stays as history.

prompt: Of the wiki's 640 pages, 410 had not been edited in two years. Teams fixed 90 of those and archived the rest. How many pages remained in the wiki?
hint: The recent pages plus the fixed ones.

prompt: Put what happened to the Payments page in order.
items: The page is written, and true
Tracking moves to its own database
Ícaro builds a report on the page
Ícaro rewrites the page with an owner and a date
trap: The page went wrong without anybody touching it: the change was in the system.

prompt: A team plans a two-week documentation sprint to fix its stale wiki. What does the lesson predict?

choices.text: The wiki stays accurate, since the pages were checked
choices.why: Checked once; the system keeps changing the next morning.

choices.text: Good pages on the last day, decay from the next
choices.why: Right: nothing in the arrangement changed, so the cause is still there.

choices.text: The team finishes in less time than planned
choices.why: Duration is beside the point.

choices.text: Readers stop trusting the wiki
choices.why: Right after the sprint they trust it more, which is the danger once it drifts.

prompt: Match each cause of rot to the arrangement that answers it.

pairs.right: a named team and person at the top

pairs.left: it lives away from the change
pairs.right: docs/ beside the code, in the same pull request
write the slow level, generate the rest
a review date and a banner when it passes

prompt: A diagram says Payments does not call Matching. How does the lesson keep that claim from going stale silently?

choices.text: The architecture forum reads it every quarter
choices.why: That is a trigger, but between quarters it could drift unnoticed.

choices.text: A program tests the claim against the code
choices.why: Right: a claim held by a test fails loudly when it stops being true.

choices.text: New engineers fix it in their first month
choices.why: Onboarding catches what misled someone, after it misled them.

choices.text: The diagram is redrawn by hand for each release
choices.why: Redrawing is effort with nothing to catch an omission.

prompt: A runbook written in 2023 for a stuck payout has no owner and nobody willing to check it. What does the lesson recommend?

choices.text: Keep it as it is, since it is a record of 2023
choices.why: A runbook describes what to do now; it is a description, not a record.

choices.text: Add a line saying "may be out of date" and leave it
choices.why: A warning with no owner behind it is a slower version of the same problem.

choices.text: Archive it, pointing at its replacement
choices.why: Right: a page that is wrong and has no owner willing to fix it should go, with a banner saying what replaced it.

choices.text: Move it to the architect's personal notes
choices.why: That hides it from the next on-call without making it right.
